limitations: Single short synthetic request per configuration, not a sustained or full-window benchmark.
The microbatch-64 run used an isolated server in the same ROCm container after unloading the production model.

Stock DPM high and then a manual PCIe-state request were applied between the runs; the reported upstream link remained Gen1 x1. The result is not a fully controlled attribution of every speed difference to microbatch alone.
The isolated ROCm llama-bench with a short context measured 559 prompt tokens/second at microbatch 512, so the GPU was capable of faster compute than the original long-context server path.
Historical 128k laptop evidence recorded approximately 817 prompt tokens/second on an 11036-token request; the Geekom does not yet match that result.
Saved configuration applies on the next backend start. End-to-end validation after the user-requested BIOS restart remains pending.
